findings.reason: The protected SQL solution normalizes product_name using LOWER(TRIM(product_name)) and extracts YYYY-MM month from sale_date using strftime('%Y-%m', sale_date). It groups by both normalized expressions, calculates COUNT(*) as total, and orders by product_name ASC, sale_date ASC. The query runs in O(r log r) time and O(g) space; no candidate is required.

Applying TRIM before LOWER eliminates leading/trailing whitespace before lowercasing, ensuring case and whitespace variants map to the same product group. Formatting sale_date as YYYY-MM correctly aggregates sales by calendar month.

Normalization is O(1) per row for r rows. Grouping and sorting g distinct groups takes O(r log r) upper bound time and O(g) auxiliary aggregation space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts Sales table and produces columns product_name, sale_date (YYYY-MM format), and total with correct ascending sort order.

The approach accurately details string trimming/lowercasing order, date formatting (YYYY-MM), GROUP BY aggregation, and O(r log r) time / O(g) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover pre-normalized computed columns, correlated count subquery overhead, whitespace removal boundaries, case-sensitivity rules, multi-month separation, zero-padded month formatting, and product-first sorting priority.

App SQL (SQLite strftime) and native SQL (MySQL DATE_FORMAT) solutions both execute the identical LOWER TRIM GROUP BY aggregation logic with SHA-256 digests 7746da68e89f66086bbca2e83122fb83baca1a8f924578abf854ea3825c2dcb9 and 977abbfba65aeb7def912d7830916a8a7b15de0a615a2694ae350d07ed97b324.
